questions.question: What does THRIVE stand for in the name of this Act?
questions.notes: Helping Small Businesses To Hedge Risk and Insure against Volatile Expenses Act.

questions.question: What does the bill say about section 1a of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 1a)?
questions.notes: Commission, commodity, commodity pool, commodity trading advisor, future delivery and futures commission merchant take their meanings from 7 U.S.C. 1a.

questions.question: Where does the bill mention the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, and why?
questions.notes: A business that is (or is owned or controlled by) a financial institution as defined in section 509 of Gramm-Leach-Bliley is not an eligible entity.

questions.question: What is a call option purchase agreement under this bill, and when does it protect a business?
questions.notes: Protects the eligible entity when the covered commodity's price rises by more than 5 percent.

questions.question: Does the bill require gasoline and diesel gasoline to be covered commodities?
questions.notes: Yes: the Administrator shall ensure they are covered commodities.

questions.question: What does the bill say about the total notional value of covered commodities?
questions.notes: Annual reports include the total notional value of covered commodities under agreements, disaggregated by commodity.

questions.question: When does the program have to start?
questions.notes: Not later than 1 year after enactment.

questions.question: Who has to pay the costs of one of these deals, and when is the first payment due?
questions.notes: The eligible entity pays all costs; initial costs are paid when it enters the agreement.

questions.question: What happens to any money the program makes?
questions.notes: Proceeds offset that fiscal year's operating costs; anything beyond goes to the general fund of the Treasury.

questions.question: Will the government ever actually take a truckload of the fuel it buys?
questions.notes: No taking delivery of any physical commodity except in extreme and exigent circumstances.

questions.question: Is there a phone line or website where a business owner can ask questions about the program?
questions.notes: Yes: outreach includes a website and telephone line for questions and help deciding whether to participate.

questions.question: How much warning do businesses get before a commodity is dropped from the program?
questions.notes: Not less than 90 days notice to participants.

questions.question: How long will the money for this program last?
questions.notes: Such sums as necessary, available until 5 years after enactment.

questions.question: Could things like electricity or natural gas be added later?
questions.notes: The Administrator must give particular consideration to classifying standard utilities such as electricity and natural gas as covered commodities.

questions.question: What is the shortest and the longest time one of these deals can last?
questions.notes: Not less than 60 days and not more than 3 years.

questions.question: Can a bank sign up for this program?
questions.notes: No: the eligible entity definition excludes financial institutions and businesses they own or control.

questions.question: My business opened six months ago. Can it apply?
questions.notes: No: businesses in operation less than 1 year when they apply are not eligible entities.

questions.question: Will the SBA share information about the program through women's business centers?
questions.notes: Outreach distributes materials through resource partners, and resource partners include women's business centers.

questions.question: Who is the Administrator that runs this program?
questions.notes: The Administrator of the Small Business Administration.

questions.question: What makes something a covered commodity?
questions.notes: A commodity the Administrator determines under section 4(b) is eligible for an agreement under section 4(a).

questions.question: Does this bill lower taxes for small businesses?
questions.notes: The bill has no tax provisions.

questions.question: What is the punishment if a business lies on its application?
questions.notes: The bill sets no penalties.

questions.question: Can a small business get a loan through this program?
questions.notes: The bill does not mention loans.
